thread:
Emma: Quick sync — working draft for live tile throttling when authz checks spike. Need short-term playbook + long-term design. Recent incident: graph-authz p95 hit ~1.2s => console tiles 503s.
Raj: Do we still prefer prefilter at the API gateway vs an inline sidecar authz call?
Emma: Prefilter helped reduce authz QPS but increased cold cache misses for tiles. It also made debugging harder.
Liam: Suggest adaptive backpressure. Measure authz latency & queue depth, then degrade low-value tiles to cached snapshots (degraded UX) instead of failing.
Taylor: Proposed short policy sketch:
```
# pseudo
if authz.p95_ms > 150 and authz.queue_len > 200:
  degrade = select(tiles) where tile.score < 0.6
  for t in degrade: route(t, cached_snapshot)
```
Taylor: Also add a telemetry flag on degraded tiles so we can track regression in metrics.
Sophie: Security note — cached snapshots must be token-bound. We cannot return cached content that was generated under a different user's effective perms. Also TTL must be short for role changes.
Liam: Right. Keying cache by (user_token_hash, tile_id, role_version) + encrypt cache entries should be minimal overhead.
Raj: Long-term idea: async authz prefetcher that warms per-user ephemeral cache during session startup. Reduces tail but increases memory and complexity.
Emma: Tradeoffs: prefetch = memory + sliding window consistency issues on role changes. But could be behind a feature flag for high-traffic tenants.
Taylor: Ops runbook action items (short-term):
- add authz p95 and queue alarms
- automated degrade toggle (manual override)
- audit logs for degraded tiles
- incident playbook steps to revert to synchronous strict path
I'll draft runbook and open PR.
deploy-bot: :rocket: canary rollout started: console/authz-degrade -> staging
Raj: I'll help with the PR for token-bound cache & review runbook.
Emma: Thanks — can Raj/Liam/Taylor review by EOD? If yes I'll merge playbook and post to #incidents-runbook.
Liam: ack, reviewing now. :thumbsup:
Sophie: I'll add the security caveats to the RFC doc and ping infra for a quick threat model.
Emma: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up tomorrow with the draft PR link.
